To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the aminovinyldene ketones of 3-hy-droxy-2-acetyIbenzo[b] thiophene are the most stable form, which undergoes reversible photochemical isomerization to the corresponding E-keto enamines, which is the most stable form of their N-alkyl- and N-aryl derivatives, and that the E-keto enamines have a low-intensity fluorescence, which is absent for the salts of their conjugate bases.
the synthesis of the title compounds was achieved, their structures were elucidated by spectroscopic methods, their photostability was investigated, and their photophysical properties were studied.

the aminovinylogous ketones are the most stable tautomers of 3-hy-droxy-2-acetyIbenzo[b]tliophenes, and the aminovine derivatives of 3-hyd-roxy-2-acetylebenzo[b]tiophene have a normal Stokesian fluorescence with a low quantum yield.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structures, and luminescence properties of aminovinil ketones and their lithium and sodium derivatives.
the synthesis, structure, and spectral properties of aminovinil ketones of 2- and 3-hydroxycarbonylbenzene derivatives, including their salts.

the synthesis, structure, spectral, and luminescence properties of the compounds with the E-keto-enamine structure, which are the first representatives of this type of compounds in the series of benzo[b]thienyl imines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the imines of 3- hydroxy-2-acetylb enzo[b] thiophene have the E-ketoenamine structure and are characterized by the presence of the tautomeric equilibrium between the enamine form of the molecule and the zwitterionic form of the enolate anion.
the 1H N-MR spectra of all the studied compounds are in agreement with the proposed E-ketoenamine structure of the imine.

the 3-hydroxycinnamoylthiophenes are a new class of compounds with a unique structure, which is characterized by the coexistence of two tautomeric forms, the keto and enamine forms, in a ratio of 3 : 2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the luminescent behavior of 3-halogen- and 3-methyl-2-acetyl-2H-benzo[b]thienyl ketimines is determined by the nature of their tautomeric equilibrium, which is shifted to the enamine form in the solid state and to the imine form in solutions.
benzo[b]-thiochroman-3-ones are the most promising compounds for the design of novel fluorescent probes for biological applications.

the luminescence of the studied compounds is determined not by the presence of the keto enamine structure, which is the most stable form of these compounds, but by the presence of a protonated amino group.

we can use the 3D-printing technique to produce a variety of complex, 3D, and highly porous materials with a range of pore sizes.
the 3-aminocrotonyl ketone structure, which is typical of the N-aryl- and N-acylimines, is the most favorable for the formation of a stable complex with lithium ions.
